fragments.text: Hello, and welcome to the fourth Artificial Intelligence for Information Accessibility Conference. And thank you very much for having us as a speaker. My name is Madeline Nolan, I'm from the Advanced Television Systems Committee. We are an international standards development organization, and I'm lucky to be here joined by Eric Langer from Information Equity Initiative and Ashish from Eon Media, who are going to talk about how AI can help with information equity to all people. So what I'd like to do is start with Eric. And tell us a little bit about Information Equity Initiative, and then we'll move to Ashish, and he can talk a little bit about how AI can help with IEI's mission and others similar

We were created a few years ago out of a recognition that about one in four U.S. households and nearly three billion people worldwide lack access to broadband, and yet television infrastructure is largely built out globally. What we've done is we've established a content platform that's interoperable in 82 percent of the world's countries using a technology called data casting so that we allow government agencies and trusted curators, like second grade teachers, public health officers, emergency managers to send curated digital content, whether that's videos, PDFs, ebooks, audio files, two homes and facilities around the world that lack access to broadband.
